oewn-11430739-n.learner: something that happens because of something that happened before it.
examples: Widely different was the effect of a second perusal.
No, Kitty, I have at least learnt to be cautious, and you will feel the effects of it.

oewn-04682671-n.learner: the way something looks from the outside.
examples: The dark curtains and low lamps gave the room a gloomy effect.

oewn-05926071-n.learner: the impression something makes on people, above all one that is put on and not natural.
examples: He paused for effect before he said the name.

oewn-00007414-r.learner: used with amounts to mean not exact but quite near the right one.

oewn-00072729-r.learner: said of moving to or among many different places, or in no set direction.
examples: The children ran about in the garden all afternoon.

oewn-00757790-v.learner: to treat something as a duty owed to you, and ask for it and expect it.
examples: Miss Bingley, however, was incapable of disappointing Mr. Darcy in anything, and persevered, therefore, in requiring an explanation of his two motives.

oewn-01036417-n.learner: a service in the Roman Catholic Church that used to be read or sung at three in the afternoon, the ninth hour counting from sunrise, and is now held a little earlier.

oewn-01561513-a.learner: the greatest number of things or people.

oewn-00063710-r.learner: in the place of something else, or as another choice in its place.

oewn-00099264-r.learner: used to say that the opposite is what is true.

oewn-01820398-v.learner: to make someone happy or pleased.
